Author: Rajasekhar Mantha
Bench: Rajasekhar Mantha
30.03.2026
Court No.13
Item No. 38-39
 pk
 F.A. 298 of 2014
 The State of West Bengal through Land Acquisition
 Collector
 Vs.
 Sujata Banerjee (since deceased) and others
 Wi T H
 C. O T. 74 of 2014
 Can 1 of 2015 (Old No. Can 2569/2015)
 Sujata Banerjee (since deceased) and others
 Vs.
 State of West Bengal
 Mr. Prasanta Kumar Giri
 Md. Zakir Hossain
 ... for the appellant-State.
 Mr. Indra Nath Mukherjee
 Mr. Tulshi Das Roy
 Mr. Avijit Saha
 ... for the private respondents
[in Fa 298 of 2014] ... for the cross objectors [in Cot 74 of 2014]
1.

The subject appeal and the cross objection are directed against Lra Case No. 20 of 2001 whereby
the learned trial Judge being learned Judge (Senior Division), Land Acquisition Court, 3rd Court at
Barasat, North 24-Parganas by order dated 28.06.2012 decided the quantum of compensation
payable to the cross-objectors/land losers.
2.  In the impugned judgment the trial Judge relied upon exemplars of three several title deeds produced by the cross-objectors/land losers and eleven title deeds produced by the State.

An average of the value of the land in the three exemplars of the cross-objectors/land losers was taken along with an average value of the eleven exemplars produced by the State and the same was divided Collector vs Sujata Banerjee (Since Deceased) And ... on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188364249/
1 by two and the trial Judge arrived at a sum of Rs.53,36,410/- as the value per acre of the cross-objectors/land losers.
3. The learned counsel for the appellant-State would argue that the trial Judge ought to have taken the only value of the exemplars produced by the State.
He further argues that as many as six of the eleven exemplars produced by the State are danga land higher in value than that of bastu land produced by the cross-objectors/land losers.

4. The learned counsel for the cross-objectors/land losers in support of his cross objection would argue that the trial Judge committed error, in considering an average price of land of any of the exemplars produced either by the State or the private respondents.

5. In terms of the dicta of the Supreme Court on the subject, it is argued by the learned counsel for the cross- objectors/land losers that the highest of the exemplars, produced both by the State as well as the private respondents, ought to have been considered by the trial Judge as land losers in an acquisition proceeding and they are entitled to the highest available value of the exemplars produced.
6. It is next argued that the interest on the assessed value of the land ought to have been calculated from 18.12.1978 being the date of actual physical possession taken by the State of the land.
Instead the learned trial Judge applied the interest of 12% from the date of issuance of notification under the Act I of L.A. Case No. LA-II/11 of 1977-78.
He further submits that the quantum of solatium awarded by the learned trial Judge would also consequently therefore, stand increased.

7. Having carefully heard the learned counsel for the appellant-State and the cross-objectors, this Court is of the view that indeed the learned trial Judge has committed error in considering the average of the value of the land in the exemplars deeds produced by the land losers as well as the State.

8. The Supreme Court of India in the case of the Mehrawal Khewaji Trust (Regd.) Faridkot & Ors. vs.
State of Punjab & Ors. reported in AIR 2012 SC 2721 held in paragraph 15 that a land looser must be given the highest value of land from the exemplars produced by the parties.

entities.text:
Mehrawal Khewaji Trust (Regd.) Faridkot & Ors. vs.
State of Punjab & Ors. reported in AIR 2012 SC 2721
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Paragraph 15 of the said judgment is quoted hereinbelow :-
"15.

It is clear that when there are several exemplars with reference to similar lands,
it is the general rule that the highest of the exemplars, if it is satisfied, that it is a bona fide transaction has to be considered and accepted.

When the land is being compulsorily taken away from a person, he is entitled to the highest value which similar land in the locality is shown to have fetched in a bona fide transaction entered into between a willing purchaser and a willing seller near about the time of the acquisition.

In our view, it seems to be only fair that where sale-deeds pertaining to different transactions are relied on behalf of the Government, the transaction representing the highest value should be preferred to the rest unless there are strong circumstances justifying a different course.

It is not desirable to take an average of Collector vs Sujata Banerjee (Since Deceased) And ... on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188364249/
2 various sale-deeds placed before the authority/court for fixing fair compensation."

9. Having regard to the aforesaid dicta, this Court is of the view that the highest value of land per acre accepted as an exhibit by the learned trial court being Rs.45,80,460/- must be the basis of calculation of compensation payable to the land losers or their legal heirs for acquisition of 0.60 acres of land in mouza -Titagarh, R.S. plot No. 812, JL No. 5, P.S. Titagarh, Dist. North 24-Parganas.

10. The interest payable on the acquired land at the value indicated hereinabove shall be calculated at 12% simple on and from 18.12.1978 till the date of the award before the trial court i.e. 15.03.2001.
The land losers or their legal heirs shall be entitled to interest post the date of award till the date of actual payment at the rate of 7% per annum.
11. The quantum of solatium payable to the land losers or their legal heirs shall correspondingly stand increased based on the value of compensation, as decided hereinabove.

12. Let the matter be remanded back to the trial Judge for recalculation and payment of compensation and quantum of interest at the rate of 12% from 18.12.1978 till 15.03.2001 and additional interest from 16.03.2001 till the date of actual payment at the rate of 7% per annum.
Let solatium also be calculated as directed hereinabove and be paid to the land losers or their legal heirs.

13. The sums deposited by the State with the Registrar General of this Court as pre-condition of the admission of the appeal shall be made over by the Registrar General to the appellants within a period of 14 days from the date of communication of a copy of this order.

14. Needless to mention the payment of compensation to the land losers or their legal heirs by the trial court shall factor in and deduct the sums directed to be paid by the Registrar General of this Court to the land losers.
15. With the aforesaid observations, the instant appeal as well as the cross-objection is disposed of.
Consequently, all pending connected applications also stand disposed of.
16. All parties shall act on a server copy of this order duly downloaded from the official website of this Court.
(Rajasekhar Mantha, J.) (Rai Chattopadhyay, J.)
